questions.text: What is the primary purpose of the passage?
options: To argue that professional scientists are no longer required
To explain citizen science and the conditions that make it useful
To warn that volunteers should not collect observations
To explain how research projects receive government funding

passage.text: Citizen science programmes invite members of the public to contribute observations to research projects. Volunteers may record birds, photograph insects, measure rainfall or report changes in local water bodies. Their contributions allow researchers to collect information across wider areas than small research teams could cover alone. However, the usefulness of such data depends on clear instructions, suitable training and methods for checking observations. When these safeguards are in place, citizen science can increase both scientific knowledge and public interest in the natural world.
